reasoning: The exact experimental protocol proposed — re-score SHADE-Arena's fixed benign/sabotage trajectories with the original monitor prompt, emit per-trajectory suspicion scores, compute per-monitor ROC/AUC, and anchor to the published Gemini 2.5 Pro AUC of 0.87 — is precisely what the original SHADE-Arena paper (Kutasov et al., arXiv:2506.15740) already does, and it already benchmarks a cheaper/weaker open-weight monitor (DeepSeek R1, AUC 0.74) alongside Gemini 2.5 Pro (0.87), Claude 3.7 (0.86), GPT-4o, and Claude 3.6. Follow-up work directly studies the same problem-level question of how close cheaper/weaker monitors get to the best closed monitor: "How does information access affect LLM monitors' ability to detect sabotage?" (arXiv:2601.21112) re-scores the same fixed trajectories with cheap models (GPT-4.1-mini, GPT-4o-mini) reporting AUCs, and "Reliable Weak-to-Strong Monitoring of LLM Agents" (arXiv:2508.19461) explicitly evaluates whether weaker monitors can oversee stronger agents on SHADE-Arena. The only minor unexplored gap is the specific consumer-GPU open-weight lineup (Llama-3.1-8B/70B, Qwen2.5-7B, Mistral-7B, Gemma-2-9B), which is a narrow engineering increment rather than a new contribution.

evidence.title: SHADE-Arena: Evaluating Sabotage and Monitoring in LLM Agents
evidence.summary: Original benchmark. Already re-scores fixed benign/sabotage trajectories with the monitor prompt and plots ROC/AUC for multiple monitors: Gemini 2.5 Pro 0.87, Claude 3.7 Sonnet 0.86, DeepSeek R1 0.74 (an open-weight monitor), plus GPT-4o and Claude 3.6 Sonnet. This is the same inference-only, fixed-trajectory re-scoring setup the proposal describes, and it already includes an open-weight monitor in the AUC comparison anchored to Gemini 0.87.

evidence.title: How does information access affect LLM monitors' ability to detect sabotage?
evidence.summary: Re-scores fixed SHADE-Arena trajectories with cheaper monitors (GPT-4.1-mini, GPT-4o-mini, Claude 3.7) and reports AUROC, log-AUROC, TPR@1%FPR. Directly addresses the problem of how cheaper monitors perform relative to the best closed monitor on the same fixed-trajectory setup, including a 'less-is-more' finding for weaker/cheaper monitors.

evidence.title: Reliable Weak-to-Strong Monitoring of LLM Agents
evidence.summary: Monitor red-teaming workflow over SHADE-Arena (and CUA-SHADE-Arena) explicitly studying whether weaker/cheaper monitors can oversee stronger agents (weak-to-strong effect), reporting AUC across threat models and anchoring to Gemini 2.5 Pro 0.87. Directly targets the proposal's problem-level question of how close a cheaper monitor can get to the best closed monitor.

evidence.title: Detecting and Evaluating Agent Sabotage
evidence.summary: Summarizes SHADE-Arena monitoring results: best monitor Gemini 2.5 Pro AUC 0.87, human annotators 0.65, and discussion that 0.87 is too low for practical deployment. Confirms the AUC-anchored monitor comparison framing the proposal would reproduce already exists publicly.
